clue.text: Hard top that could make vehicle fast

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly, at speed

explanation.surface: A hard roof that might turn a car into a quick one.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crab, a protective top.

clue.text: Careless sixty per cent of victims

indicators.note: only six of the ten letters remain, the last four being dropped

parts.note: casualties are victims of an accident or war

explanation.surface: A careless attack injures most of the victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means offhand or careless.

clue.text: Weaken fast, held down by soldiers

indicators.note: in a down entry the soldiers' letters sit on top, pressing the fast below

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A soldier pinned down by his comrades begins to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or ease off from a hard position.

clue.text: Turn to bigwig after being set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the letters are reversed to read upwards
the bigwig comes after the word to

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A big shot turns away after being framed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to swivel or rotate on a point.

clue.text: Group pressure finally comes after erotic dancing

indicators.note: the final letter is placed behind the jumbled word
the word erotic dances about into a new order
only the last letter of pressure is taken

explanation.surface: A crowd feels pressure after some racy dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people.

clue.text: Marched in a line, crossing motorway, and shot

indicators.note: the marching line passes over the road, so the word for marching goes round its letter

parts.note: to file is to walk in single file
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched in single file across a motorway and were gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire, but here it is the film-making sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the cinematic sense means recorded on camera.

clue.text: I am quick, posh and unrehearsed

parts.note: contracted to I'm
prompt means quick
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A boastful speaker claims to be sharp, classy and spontaneous.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done without preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Sweet provided by charmer in guesthouse?

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the run of clue words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A dessert served by a smooth-talking host at a B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a dessert of baked whisked egg white and sugar.

clue.text: Justifies low exam grades and answers

parts.note: D and E are poor marks
serves means answers a need or purpose

explanation.surface: Poor marks explain why a student's answers fall short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that deserves an outcome merits or warrants it.

clue.text: Disposal must cover one barrel for water

indicators.note: the outer word wraps over the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a sale is a disposal of goods
I is the Roman numeral one
a vat is a large barrel or tub

explanation.surface: A clearance sale has to include a single barrel meant for holding water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' looks like a noun but is a verb, as when the mouth waters.
explanation.definitionFit: When the mouth waters it produces spit, which is to salivate.

clue.text: Cuts back on seconds and extras

indicators.note: the trimming word is placed on, after, the seconds abbreviation

parts.note: to pare is to trim or reduce

explanation.surface: A cost-cutter trims second helpings and other extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Spares are additional items kept in reserve, surplus ones beyond what is needed.

clue.text: This is the answer!

parts.note: the solution is the word for what the solver reads to get each entry, turning the usual relation round

explanation.surface: A triumphant cry on cracking a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Each crossword answer is what its hint leads to, so the hint is what the answer answers.

clue.text: Uncooked tuna — a rule that's broken

indicators.note: a broken rule is shattered, so its letters with the others are rearranged

explanation.surface: Serving tuna raw breaks some kitchen rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English for food served plain or raw, without cooking.

clue.text: Widow nervously entertaining holder of title

indicators.note: the two words play host to the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A nervous widow hosts the person who holds a noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of the title deeds to property is its legal proprietor.

clue.text: Follow when husband leaves, for instance

indicators.note: the husband's letter departs from the word for following

parts.note: to chase is to follow in pursuit

explanation.surface: Someone tails a wife once her husband goes out, say.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an instance or example, as in 'a case in point'.

clue.text: A star dancing with Prince in Asia will find material

indicators.note: the letters of a star dance into a new order

parts.note: a khan is a ruler or prince in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A celebrity dancing with an Asian prince picks out some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a curly lamb's-wool fabric, named after a Russian city.

clue.text: Support European partner

parts.note: a spouse is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: Backing given to a partner from the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and back it.

clue.text: Mistakes of line taken by post-war generation

indicators.note: the line's letter is taken into the generation's word

parts.note: baby boomers were born after the Second World War

explanation.surface: Errors made by baby boomers in their approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers is an informal British word for blunders.

clue.text: Seeing some burglar get nicked on the way up is essential

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters read upwards, reversed
only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: Seeing a burglar arrested while climbing up is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGETNI is taken from 'burglar get nicked' and read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means fundamental, necessary to the whole.

clue.text: Broadcaster's connected with American medicinal preparation

indicators.note: what a broadcaster says is heard over the air rather than seen in print

parts.note: linked means connected, joined to; US is short for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: A radio presenter is tied up with a US cough remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.

clue.text: Humiliation? Mostly pretence

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, the final letter dropped

parts.note: shame is humiliation

explanation.surface: Is the embarrassment largely put on?
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake or deception.

clue.text: Not quite satisfied, having eaten nothing disgusting

indicators.note: the shortened word swallows the zero, taking it inside
the word for satisfied loses its final letter

parts.note: full means satisfied after a meal
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Still a bit hungry after eating nothing revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul means vile or revolting.

clue.text: Prefer to accommodate Liberal character

indicators.note: the word for prefer houses the Liberal's letter

parts.note: to favour is to prefer

explanation.surface: Choosing to make room for a Liberal personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavour means distinctive quality or character, as in the flavour of a place.

clue.text: One of five, in the borders of Europe, like a horse

indicators.note: the quintuplet goes between the two border letters
the outside letters of Europe are taken

parts.note: a quin is a quintuplet, one of five born together

explanation.surface: One of five siblings on the edges of Europe resembles a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to or resembling horses.

clue.text: Fed up with European Commission? Time to change allegiance

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: EC is the European Commission

explanation.surface: Tired of Brussels? It's time to switch sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as one phrase meaning annoyed; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to desert one's country or party for another.

clue.text: Letter should give order date for return

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: the word for a date is sent back, read in the other direction

parts.note: an age is a period or era, a date in history

explanation.surface: A letter should state the date by which goods must be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Ballet position of sailor in lively square beginning to evolve

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the word square is jumbled about in a lively way

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: only the opening letter of evolve is taken

explanation.surface: A dancing sailor takes up a pose in a busy town square as the routine develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like part of the scene but is the fodder; 'lively' jumbles it to ARESQU, which the sailor sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a classic dance pose on one leg with the other extended behind.

clue.text: Speak highly of former tax cut

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the word for tax is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a toll is a levy or tax

explanation.surface: Praise a former tax reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically.

clue.text: Crude description of our world?

definitions.meaning: coarse or vulgar, especially in humour
like the planet we live on, read as earth with -y

explanation.surface: A vulgar remark about the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down to earth, and the word also means of the planet.

clue.text: Manage development of voiceprint without IP

indicators.note: the remaining letters develop into a new arrangement
the letters of IP are taken away from voiceprint

explanation.surface: A tech firm builds voice-recognition software without its intellectual property.
explanation.walkthrough: IP usually means intellectual property; here it is just the two letters I and P, leaving VOCERINT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrive to do something is to manage it by ingenuity.

clue.text: Saying nothing as is head of psychology, for example

definitions.text: as is head of psychology, for example
definitions.meaning: the opening P of psychology is not pronounced

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped head of the psychology department.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent means quiet, and is also the term for a letter written but not pronounced.

clue.text: Most amusing list set out by Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a roll is a register or list

indicators.note: set out means the word set is laid out in a different order

explanation.surface: The funniest list was compiled by Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly funny, and this is its superlative.
